summary: Learners build fluency with P(event) = favourable outcomes / total outcomes for equally-likely situations, giving answers as fractions in simplest form. The core routine is: check the outcomes are equally likely, count favourable outcomes, count the TOTAL (which includes the favourable ones), form the fraction, and simplify. Practice should span varied contexts (dice, bags, spinners) and target the part-part error (favourable-to-unfavourable) and the misapplication of the formula to unequal outcomes.
misconceptions: Writing favourable-to-unfavourable (part-part) instead of favourable-over-total — e.g. 3/7 rather than 3/10 for 3 blue among 10
Applying the formula to situations whose outcomes are not equally likely (an uneven spinner, a weighted die)
Failing to simplify, or simplifying incorrectly
Miscounting the total — forgetting to include the favourable outcomes in the denominator

activities.title: Varied probability ladder with simplest form
steps: Work a short series of problems, each a probability to be formed and then simplified: (a) a bag of 3 blue and 7 red marbles \u2014 find P(blue); (b) a fair six-sided die \u2014 find P(rolling a 4); (c) a spinner with 8 equal sections, 2 of them gold \u2014 find P(gold).
For each item, first confirm the outcomes are equally likely, then count the favourable outcomes, then count the WHOLE set of possible outcomes (including the favourable ones) for the denominator.
Write each probability as a fraction and simplify where possible (e.g. 2/8 \u2192 1/4).
On the bag item, if you write 3/7, stop and recount: the denominator is all 10 marbles, including the 3 blue ones, so the answer is 3/10.
Encounter at least one unequal-outcome situation (e.g. an uneven spinner with different-sized sections) and decide whether the simple formula applies before using it.
activities.insight: The denominator is the whole set of equally-likely outcomes, favourable included \u2014 so P(blue) among 3 blue and 7 red is 3/10, not 3/7. The simple favourable/total formula only applies when outcomes are equally likely, and simplifying (2/8 = 1/4) names the same point on the 0-to-1 scale.

activities.title: Editable bag: watch the fraction form and simplify
steps: Edit the composition of a bag (e.g. add or remove blue and red counters) and read the probability fraction as it forms.
Identify the WHOLE set as the denominator each time the bag changes, confirming favourable counters are part of that total.
Watch the simplified form of the fraction and a marker on a 0-to-1 line move as the composition changes.
Predict: 'If I add 5 more red marbles, which number in the fraction changes, and does P(blue) go up or down?' then check against the live display.
activities.insight: More favourable outcomes relative to the whole set raise the probability; the denominator is always the whole outcome set. Seeing the fraction and its position on the scale update as the bag changes connects composition to the value of the probability.

activities.title: Worked example and Socratic 'out of how many?' check
steps: Study a worked die or bag example: identify the favourable outcomes, then the whole set, then reveal the simplified fraction.
When asked 'and out of how many altogether?', state the full count of possible outcomes, not just the non-favourable ones.
Explain in your own words why the total includes the favourable outcomes.
activities.insight: Articulating the total as the whole set (favourable included) catches the part-part slip before it becomes a habit and makes the structure of the formula explicit.

checkQuestion: Give the child three problems on cards with paper: (a) a bag of 3 blue and 7 red marbles — find P(blue); (b) a fair six-sided die — find P(rolling a 4); (c) a spinner with 8 equal sections, 2 of them gold — find P(gold). Say: 'Work out each probability and write it as a fraction in its simplest form.' (Set the task and WATCH — watch whether they count the TOTAL correctly, whether they check the outcomes are equally likely, and whether they simplify.)
checkAnswer: A correct performance: (a) P(blue) = 3/10 — three favourable out of ten counters altogether, blue included in the total; (b) P(4) = 1/6; (c) P(gold) = 2/8 = 1/4 simplified. The child forms favourable/TOTAL each time, puts the whole set in the denominator, and simplifies where possible.
